claim: The alpha/B.1.1.7 SARS-CoV-2 lineage emerged in autumn 2020 in the United Kingdom.
source: The alpha/B.1.1.7 SARS-CoV-2 lineage emerged in autumn 2020 in the United Kingdom and transmitted rapidly until winter 2021 when it was responsible for most new COVID-19 cases in many European countries.
evidence: This is a statement about the temporal and geographic origin of the variant, drawing from established knowledge and likely supported by surveillance data.

claim: The alpha/B.1.1.7 variant transmitted rapidly until winter 2021 when it was responsible for most new COVID-19 cases in many European countries.
source: The alpha/B.1.1.7 SARS-CoV-2 lineage emerged in autumn 2020 in the United Kingdom and transmitted rapidly until winter 2021 when it was responsible for most new COVID-19 cases in many European countries.
evidence: This statement about transmission patterns and case dominance is based on epidemiological knowledge and surveillance data.

claim: The incidence domination of alpha/B.1.1.7 was likely due to a fitness advantage that could be driven by the receptor-binding domain (RBD) residue change (N501Y).
source: The incidence domination was likely due to a fitness advantage that could be driven by the receptor-binding domain (RBD) residue change (N501Y), which also emerged independently in other variants of concern such as the beta/B.1.351 and gamma/P.1 strains.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism underlying the variant's dominance, indicated by the word 'likely'.

claim: The N501Y mutation emerged independently in other variants of concern such as the beta/B.1.351 and gamma/P.1 strains.
source: The incidence domination was likely due to a fitness advantage that could be driven by the receptor-binding domain (RBD) residue change (N501Y), which also emerged independently in other variants of concern such as the beta/B.1.351 and gamma/P.1 strains.
evidence: This statement about convergent evolution is based on genomic surveillance knowledge.

claim: The alpha/B.1.1.7 variant shows an eightfold affinity increase towards human angiotensin-converting enzyme-2 (ACE-2).
source: Here, we present a functional characterization of the alpha/B.1.1.7 variant and show an eightfold affinity increase towards human angiotensin-converting enzyme-2 (ACE-2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from biolayer interferometry measurements presented in the manuscript.

claim: Transgenic hACE2 mice showed a faster disease progression and severity after infection with a low dose of B.1.1.7, compared to an early 2020 SARS-CoV-2 isolate.
source: In accordance with this, transgenic hACE2 mice showed a faster disease progression and severity after infection with a low dose of B.1.1.7, compared to an early 2020 SARS-CoV-2 isolate.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the K18-hACE2 mouse model presented in the manuscript.

claim: The N501Y variant showed a minor, but significant elevated evasion potential of ACE-2/RBD antibody neutralization when challenged with sera from convalescent individuals.
source: When challenged with sera from convalescent individuals or anti-RBD monoclonal antibodies, the N501Y variant showed a minor, but significant elevated evasion potential of ACE-2/RBD antibody neutralization.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from antibody inhibition assays with convalescent sera.

claim: The N501Y variant showed a minor, but significant elevated evasion potential of ACE-2/RBD antibody neutralization when challenged with anti-RBD monoclonal antibodies.
source: When challenged with sera from convalescent individuals or anti-RBD monoclonal antibodies, the N501Y variant showed a minor, but significant elevated evasion potential of ACE-2/RBD antibody neutralization.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from antibody inhibition assays with monoclonal antibodies.

claim: The single asparagine to tyrosine substitution remarkable rise in affinity may be responsible for the higher transmission rate and severity of the B.1.1.7 variant.
source: The data suggest that the single asparagine to tyrosine substitution remarkable rise in affinity may be responsible for the higher transmission rate and severity of the B.1.1.7 variant.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on inference from the experimental data presented, indicated by 'suggest' and 'may be'.

claim: The spike protein binds directly to the angiotensin-converting enzyme-2 (ACE-2) receptor responsible for viral entry into the human host cells.
source: These mutations have received much attention since the spike protein binds directly to the angiotensin-converting enzyme-2 (ACE-2) receptor responsible for viral entry into the human host cells (Hoffmann et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2020; Walls et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Almost all current vaccine formulations, except for the few vaccines that rely on the inactivated SARS-CoV-2, focus on raising immunity specifically towards the spike protein or parts of it, mostly the receptor-binding domain (RBD).
source: Furthermore, almost all current vaccine formulations, except for the few vaccines that rely on the inactivated SARS-CoV-2, focus on raising immunity specifically towards the spike protein or parts of it, mostly the receptor-binding domain (RBD) (Krammer, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and represents knowledge about vaccine design strategies.

claim: Several of the non-synonymous mutations identified to date are located in the RBD of the spike protein and may improve viral fitness by raising the affinity of the virus towards ACE-2 or by hindering antibody-mediated viral neutralization.
source: In fact, several of the non-synonymous mutations identified to date are located in the RBD of the spike protein and may improve viral fitness by raising the affinity of the virus towards ACE-2 or by hindering antibody-mediated viral neutralization (Dao et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and involves speculation about mechanisms of viral fitness improvement.

claim: The N501Y mutation seems to have arisen independently by convergent evolution and selection and is found in the B.1.1.7 (alpha), the South African B.1.351 (beta), and the Brazilian P.1 (gamma) variants of concern (VOC).
source: Some of these residue substitutions, including the N501Y mutation, seem to have arisen independently by convergent evolution and selection and are found in the B.1.1.7 (alpha), the South African B.1.351 (beta), and the Brazilian P.1 (gamma) variants of concern (VOC) (Rambaut, 2020; Faria et al., 2021; Tegally et al., 2021) as well as the variant of interest (VOI) B.1.621 (mu), first identified in Colombia (Laiton-Donato et al., 2021), and the former VOI P.3 (theta) from The Philippines (Tablizo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to genomic surveillance studies.

claim: The N501Y mutation is found in the variant of interest (VOI) B.1.621 (mu), first identified in Colombia.
source: Some of these residue substitutions, including the N501Y mutation, seem to have arisen independently by convergent evolution and selection and are found in the B.1.1.7 (alpha), the South African B.1.351 (beta), and the Brazilian P.1 (gamma) variants of concern (VOC) (Rambaut, 2020; Faria et al., 2021; Tegally et al., 2021) as well as the variant of interest (VOI) B.1.621 (mu), first identified in Colombia (Laiton-Donato et al., 2021), and the former VOI P.3 (theta) from The Philippines (Tablizo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a study on the mu variant.

claim: The N501Y mutation is found in the former VOI P.3 (theta) from The Philippines.
source: Some of these residue substitutions, including the N501Y mutation, seem to have arisen independently by convergent evolution and selection and are found in the B.1.1.7 (alpha), the South African B.1.351 (beta), and the Brazilian P.1 (gamma) variants of concern (VOC) (Rambaut, 2020; Faria et al., 2021; Tegally et al., 2021) as well as the variant of interest (VOI) B.1.621 (mu), first identified in Colombia (Laiton-Donato et al., 2021), and the former VOI P.3 (theta) from The Philippines (Tablizo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a study on the theta variant.

claim: All the VOC containing N501Y have been for the most part replaced by the B.1.617.2 (delta), which emerged in India in December 2020.
source: All the above VOC/VOI have been for the most part replaced by the B.1.617.2 (delta), which emerged in India in December 2020 (Cherian et al., 2021; Yadav, 2021) and has become the dominant variant globally (http://www.gisaid.org/, accessed October 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations and reference to GISAID surveillance data.

claim: The B.1.617.2 (delta) variant has become the dominant variant globally.
source: All the above VOC/VOI have been for the most part replaced by the B.1.617.2 (delta), which emerged in India in December 2020 (Cherian et al., 2021; Yadav, 2021) and has become the dominant variant globally (http://www.gisaid.org/, accessed October 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations and reference to GISAID surveillance data.

claim: A not-yet-peer reviewed publication on vaccine breakthrough found that the N501Y mutation was associated with increased number of breakthrough infections.
source: A not-yet-peer reviewed publication on vaccine breakthrough, found that the N501Y mutation was associated with increased number of breakthrough infections (Marques et al., 2021).

claim: Recent studies suggest that the B.1.1.7, B.1.351, P.1, and B.1.617.2 VOC have increased transmissibility.
source: Recent studies suggest that the B.1.1.7, B.1.351, P.1, and B.1.617.2 VOC have increased transmissibility (Faria et al., 2021; Tegally et al., 2021; Davies et al., 2021a; Kidd et al., 2021; Scientific Pandemic Influenza Group on Modelling Operational sub-group (SPI-M-O), 2021) and appear to cause a more severe disease (Davies et al., 2021b; Funk et al., 2021; Pearson, 2021; Sheikh et al., 2021), albeit most rely primarily on epidemiological and prediction data.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to epidemiological studies.

claim: The B.1.1.7, B.1.351, P.1, and B.1.617.2 VOC appear to cause a more severe disease.
source: Recent studies suggest that the B.1.1.7, B.1.351, P.1, and B.1.617.2 VOC have increased transmissibility (Faria et al., 2021; Tegally et al., 2021; Davies et al., 2021a; Kidd et al., 2021; Scientific Pandemic Influenza Group on Modelling Operational sub-group (SPI-M-O), 2021) and appear to cause a more severe disease (Davies et al., 2021b; Funk et al., 2021; Pearson, 2021; Sheikh et al., 2021), albeit most rely primarily on epidemiological and prediction data.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to epidemiological studies, though the authors note these rely on epidemiological and prediction data.

claim: The B.1.351, P.1, and B.1.617.2 variants have a reduced potential of antibody-dependent virus neutralization from convalescent individuals.
source: Moreover, other reports indicate that especially the B.1.351, P.1, and B.1.617.2 have a reduced potential of antibody-dependent virus neutralization from convalescent individuals and might pose a challenge to current vaccines (Wu et al., 2021; Madhi et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2021b; Zhou et al., 2021; Dejnirattisai et al., 2021; Cele et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to neutralization studies.

claim: The B.1.351, P.1, and B.1.617.2 variants might pose a challenge to current vaccines.
source: Moreover, other reports indicate that especially the B.1.351, P.1, and B.1.617.2 have a reduced potential of antibody-dependent virus neutralization from convalescent individuals and might pose a challenge to current vaccines (Wu et al., 2021; Madhi et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2021b; Zhou et al., 2021; Dejnirattisai et al., 2021; Cele et al., 2021).

source: The same immune evasion capacity has not been reported for the B.1.1.7 variant, although some evasion cannot be excluded (Supasa et al., 2021).

source: A large yeast two-hybrid study characterizing the mutational landscape of SARS-CoV-2 RBD indicated that the N501Y residue-change results in increased affinity towards ACE-2 (Starr et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Two recent studies have focused on the N501Y mutation showing a variable impact on affinity (from 0.5 nM to sub pM).
source: Two recent studies, one still non-peer reviewed, have focused on the N501Y mutation showing a variable impact on affinity (from 0.5 nM to sub pM) (Tian et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to two studies.

claim: The 1:1 interaction affinity of N439K to human ACE-2 is twofold increased compared to the original Wuhan RBD.
source: In the present study, we have performed detailed biophysical characterization of the RBD variants N439K (the most prevalent RBD mutation to date) and N501Y (shared between the B.1.1.7, B.1.351, and P.1), showing that the 1:1 interaction affinity to human ACE-2 is two- and eightfold increased, respectively, compared to the original Wuhan RBD.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from biolayer interferometry measurements.

claim: The 1:1 interaction affinity of N501Y to human ACE-2 is eightfold increased compared to the original Wuhan RBD.
source: In the present study, we have performed detailed biophysical characterization of the RBD variants N439K (the most prevalent RBD mutation to date) and N501Y (shared between the B.1.1.7, B.1.351, and P.1), showing that the 1:1 interaction affinity to human ACE-2 is two- and eightfold increased, respectively, compared to the original Wuhan RBD.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from biolayer interferometry measurements.

claim: A lower infection dose was required to establish infection when challenged with the alpha/B.1.1.7 variant compared to an early 2020 isolate in transgenic humanized ACE-2 mouse model.
source: Using a transgenic humanized ACE-2 mouse model we found that a lower infection dose was required to establish infection when challenged with the alpha/B.1.1.7 variant compared to an early 2020 isolate (differing at the N501Y position) and that the alpha variant resulted in increased disease severity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the K18-hACE2 mouse model.

claim: The alpha variant resulted in increased disease severity in transgenic humanized ACE-2 mouse model.
source: Using a transgenic humanized ACE-2 mouse model we found that a lower infection dose was required to establish infection when challenged with the alpha/B.1.1.7 variant compared to an early 2020 isolate (differing at the N501Y position) and that the alpha variant resulted in increased disease severity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the K18-hACE2 mouse model.

claim: There was a statistically significant reduction in the inhibition of the N439K RBD compared to the wt in sera of recovered COVID-19 patients (n = 140).
source: To do so, we first determined the antibody-mediated inhibition potency, measured as the inhibition of the ACE-2/RBD interaction, in sera of recovered COVID-19 patients (n = 140) using a validated in vitro antibody inhibition assay (Bayarri-Olmos et al., 2021a; Figure 3A–C). There was a statistically significant reduction in the inhibition of the N439K and N501Y RBD compared to the wt (p < 0.0001 for both) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from antibody inhibition assays shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There was a statistically significant reduction in the inhibition of the N501Y RBD compared to the wt in sera of recovered COVID-19 patients (n = 140).
source: To do so, we first determined the antibody-mediated inhibition potency, measured as the inhibition of the ACE-2/RBD interaction, in sera of recovered COVID-19 patients (n = 140) using a validated in vitro antibody inhibition assay (Bayarri-Olmos et al., 2021a; Figure 3A–C). There was a statistically significant reduction in the inhibition of the N439K and N501Y RBD compared to the wt (p < 0.0001 for both) (Figure 3A).

claim: The inhibition potencies towards the wt and the N439K variant had a highly significant correlation (ρ = 0.9774, p < 0.0001).
source: The inhibition potencies towards the wt and the variants had a highly significant correlation (ρ = 0.9774 and ρ = 0.9581 for N439K and N501Y, respectively, p < 0.0001), with the best-fit X-intercept ranging from 12.38 to 15.89 for the N439K and N501Y, respectively (Figure 3B, C).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The inhibition potencies towards the wt and the N501Y variant had a highly significant correlation (ρ = 0.9581, p < 0.0001).

claim: The N439K variant has a ~2.5°C reduction in the inflection temperature (Ti) compared to wild-type RBD.
source: We monitored the thermal unfolding using the intrinsic fluorescence ratio at 350 and 330 nm and observed a ~2.5°C reduction in the inflection temperature (Ti) for the N439K variant (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from thermal stability measurements shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The N439K variant has a moderately deleterious effect on the RBD stability.
source: This suggests that the N439K, but not the N501Y, has a moderately deleterious effect on the RBD stability.

claim: The N439K variant bound to ACE-2 with an approximately twofold higher affinity than the wt (8.6 vs 17 nM).

claim: The N501Y variant bound to ACE-2 with an eightfold higher affinity than the wt (2.23 vs 17 nM).

claim: The N439K variant bound to ACE-2 faster than wt (KaN439K = 4.15 × 10^5 M^−1 s^−1, Kawt = 3.34 × 10^5 M^−1 s^−1).

source: However, although many spike variants have been reported so far, there seems to be a limitation in terms of the 'freedom' possibilities to which and how many non-synonymous mutations are emerging in the S gene and particularly in the RBD coding region (Starr et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an inference based on observation of mutation patterns, supported by a citation.

claim: The B.1.617.2 (delta) variant does not contain the N501Y mutation.
source: One of these RBD residue changes is N501Y, which has appeared by convergent evolution in three of the so-called VOC: B.1.351 (beta), P.1 (gamma), and the B.1.1.7 (alpha) variant, but interestingly not in the rapidly spreading B.1.617.2 (delta) variant, where other mutations appear to be of importance.
evidence: This is stated explicitly in the text and represents genomic surveillance knowledge.

claim: In the B.1.617.2 (delta) variant, mutations other than N501Y appear to be of importance for viral fitness.
source: One of these RBD residue changes is N501Y, which has appeared by convergent evolution in three of the so-called VOC: B.1.351 (beta), P.1 (gamma), and the B.1.1.7 (alpha) variant, but interestingly not in the rapidly spreading B.1.617.2 (delta) variant, where other mutations appear to be of importance.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from the observation that delta lacks N501Y but still spreads rapidly.

claim: The B.1.1.7 (alpha) variant was dominating many European countries at the end of March 2021.
source: In Europe, the B.1.1.7 (alpha) variant was, at the end of March 2021, dominating many countries only few months after its emergence with severe consequences on the health care system, while now just a few months later in the end of August 2021, the B1.617.2 (delta) variant has taken over (http://www.gisaid.com/, accessed August 2021).
evidence: This is based on surveillance data from GISAID.

claim: The B1.617.2 (delta) variant has taken over from B.1.1.7 in Europe by the end of August 2021.
source: In Europe, the B.1.1.7 (alpha) variant was, at the end of March 2021, dominating many countries only few months after its emergence with severe consequences on the health care system, while now just a few months later in the end of August 2021, the B1.617.2 (delta) variant has taken over (http://www.gisaid.com/, accessed August 2021).
evidence: This is based on surveillance data from GISAID.

claim: The eightfold affinity increase of N501Y RBD to ACE-2 might be a central explanation for the observed higher transmission rate and the fitness advantage of the B.1.1.7 variant.
source: When we did BLI measurements of the 1:1 interaction of N501Y RBD on ACE-2 immobilized sensors, we found a remarkable eightfold affinity increase of the variant (2.2 nM) compared to wt Wuhan RBD (17 nM). This might be a central explanation for the observed higher transmission rate and the fitness advantage of the B.1.1.7 variant.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on inference from the experimental affinity data, indicated by 'might be'.

claim: The 1:1 molecular affinity determination might underestimate the true in vivo interaction potential covering multivalent avidity interactions between the trimeric spike scaffolds on the viral surface and the ACE-2-covered host membrane.
source: Furthermore, the 1:1 molecular affinity determination might even underestimate the true in vivo interaction potential covering multivalent avidity interactions between the trimeric spike scaffolds on the viral surface and the ACE-2-covered host membrane.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on reasoning about the difference between in vitro and in vivo conditions.

claim: The B.1.1.7 variant might also infect WT mice though not as efficient as the P.1 and B.1.351.
source: Another report has shown that the B.1.1.7 variant might also infect WT mice though not as efficient as the P.1 and B.1.351 (Tian et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to another study.

claim: Two recent studies reported affinities of N501Y ranging from 0.5 nM to undefined sub pM, using immobilized RBD incubated with dimeric ACE-2 in the soluble phase.
source: Two recent studies, one yet-to-be peer reviewed, have focused on the biophysics of the N501Y variant, reporting affinities ranging from 0.5 nM (Tian et al., 2021) to undefined sub pM (Liu et al., 2021a).
